_comment: Fragment 43 — D-90: the handoff channel, Lane B's feedback path. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-90 — The Handoff Channel: Lane B Can Speak Without Crossing
nodes.description: Creates docs/handoff/ as the location D-75 required and never named, plus C-14 check 10. One file per entry, four kinds — dependency, spec-defect, blocked-on-decision, finding — and three dispositions: Acknowledged, Answered, Withdrawn.
nodes.rationale: Lane B's surface holds nothing in docs, so reporting a spec defect or a blocked dependency meant editing docs, which is an A plus B crossing the commit gate now blocks. The gate installed one commit earlier would have blocked the first thing Lane B tried to say.

nodes.label: The Channel Belongs to No Lane, On Purpose
nodes.description: The instruction was a Lane-B-owned directory. Implemented as unmapped instead, because under Lane B ownership Lane A's reply becomes a crossing on every ordinary use: a response normally lands with the doc update that answers it, which is Lane A's surface. The channel would fight the gate on the flow it exists to serve.
nodes.rationale: The principle this register settled twice already. G63: a per-file merge rule cannot fit a file carrying two kinds of content. D-85: package.json carries Lane A scripts and Lane B dependencies, so attributing it to one misclassifies the other half. A genuinely joint surface should not be attributed to one owner.

nodes.label: The Check Requires Acknowledgement, Not a Fast Answer
nodes.description: Check 10 fails on an open entry with no Lane A disposition, on a malformed entry, and on an Answered status with an empty response. It deliberately passes on an open entry that has been acknowledged.
nodes.rationale: A queue is healthy. Failing on one would make bun run check red whenever Lane B has a pending request, and a check that is red in the normal case is a check people stop reading. This is the same reasoning D-83 used to make lane-boundary report a crossing rather than forbid one.

nodes.label: One File Per Entry, Because a Log Would Mix Content Kinds
nodes.description: Entries are separate files named B-NNN-slug.md rather than appended to a shared log. docs/handoff/ falls under the union merge attribute, which is correct for append-only entries and wrong for the current-value Status field a shared log would carry.
nodes.rationale: The mixed-file trap G63 recorded, applied before it could happen rather than after. Modular_PRD and the register each carry append-only and current-value content together, which is why no per-file merge rule fits them.
